parts:
Kylie, 

I am a huge fan of your work and of Cardinal. I have been reading the Help pages about the "select" command in order to subset your data and remove the background. However, whenever I use this command it seems like clicking on the image gives no input. The cursor does not change to an arrow and the image does not seem be interactive, or "executable." Berkley Ellis

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Select Command
parts:
Hi Berkley,

Unfortunately, this is a problem with RStudio. Because of the way RStudio displays plots, the graphics::locator() function that Cardinal relies on for select() has trouble updating the plot. The function will still work and return the selection correctly (although I believe you'll need to hit RStudio's "stop" button instead of ESC), but you'll have to do it "blind" as drawing the points/lines doesn't work in RStudio. It should work fine if you try it in the R application rather than RStudio.

I had hoped RStudio would fix this functionality on their own, as it is used by many more packages besides Cardinal, but I may have to think about creating a workaround at some point.

-Kylie

messages.author: db2a70d9b31cb1f7
messages.subject: Re: Select Command
parts:
Hey Jack,

the select function does not give you a new image subset but only the information if the pixel is in your ROI or not (logical vector with TRUE and FALSE for each pixel). You need a second step in which you filter your imaging data for the pixels which are TRUE (within your ROI):

ROI_pixels = select(msidata, mode="region", colorkey=FALSE) #select ROI
ROI_image = msidata[,ROI_pixels] # subset original dataset for ROI
image(ROI_image, mz=1) # visual control

Best,
Melanie
